chunks: And with this chain of narration, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from al-Hasan ibn al-Sariy, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'I narrate a hadith to a man, and he goes off and narrates it from me just as he heard it, so I make permissible cursing him and disassociating from him because of it.'
ai.seo_question: Why did Imam al-Sadiq curse those who spread his hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) illustrates the gravity of *al-ghayba* (preserving the secret) by noting that indiscriminate dissemination of his teachings by the unqualified warrants his cursing and disassociation, a practice rooted in the Prophetic tradition of distinguishing between the worthy and the unworthy. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on *tadlis* (concealment) not merely as hiding facts, but as a protective measure to preserve the integrity and depth of religious knowledge from distortion by those lacking the requisite spiritual or intellectual capacity.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (7) The same previous series of narrators from al-Hasan bin Ali bin Abu Hamza from al-Hasan as-Sariy

that Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (as) had said: “When I tell someone a tradition and he spreads it as he hears it from me, he will deserve to be cursed and repudiated.”
He meant that if that someone would spread the tradition among those who were not reliable or qualified. Imam as-Sadiq’s saying showed that he wanted some of the traditions to be kept secret and not to be spread.
